message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze this situation carefully.

The position: Rhea Lend (ex-Burrow) on NEAR, contract.main.burrow.near, supplies native USDC (~$1,000), no debt. So the user is a supplier of USDC on this lending market.

Timeline of observations:

- O01 (Apr 15 22:48): 21 implicit accounts deleted, same beneficiary, funded via intents.near. None interacted with burrow contract. This is suspicious precursor activity — attacker infrastructure being set up. Not directly touching the position.

- O02 (Apr 16 07:59): Normal state. USDC utilization 74.84%, all can_withdraw=true.

- O03 (08:15): USDC reserve fell 32% during margin-position swap settlement. Utilization 75.18%.

- O04 (08:21): Official team says discrepancies are monitor-indexing delay during scheduled maintenance, contracts fully backed, withdrawals normal, "please keep positions open." This is a reassurance that later proved false — classic pattern during an exploit (team says everything fine while drain ongoing). Note: official communications during active incidents saying "funds are safe" should be discounted when onchain data contradicts.

- O05 (08:22): margin_execute_with_pyth OpenPosition calls from fresh implicit accounts (<48h old), swap routes through Ref pools created minutes earlier. This matches the attack pattern CertiK later described: fake token contracts + fresh pools misleading oracle/validation.

- O06 (08:45): USDC held fell to 5.12M vs ledger-available 7.09M (72%). Reserve nearly wiped (73.7k from 372k). Supplied jumped. This is the beginning of the drain — held balance diverging from ledger accounting.

- O07 (08:50): USDC held 3.34M vs ledger 7.62M (44%). USDT held 41%. Outflow ~1.8M per 5 min per asset. Reserve 0.

- O08 (08:52): Account creates 5 fake pools on Ref with unnamed implicit-account token contracts, zero/odd fees, then storage_deposits on burrow. Attack setup confirmed onchain.

- O09 (08:55): Same account opens margin position on burrow using the fake pools as swap route. This is the exploit transaction pattern.

- O10 (09:00): USDC held 0.88M vs ledger 8.67M (10%). USDT 10%. wNEAR starting to drop. ZEC dropping.

- O11 (09:10): USDC held 4.8% of ledger. wNEAR 59% and falling fast.

- O12 (09:35): wNEAR held 0.35% of ledger — essentially fully drained. USDC held 0.667M vs 9.59M ledger (7%).

- O13 (09:44): Margin activity stops. USDC held 0.82M vs 9.74M ledger (~8.4%). can_withdraw still true.

- O14 (09:54): Guardian disables wrap.near capacities.

- O15 (09:54:46): Guardian disables native USDC (all capacities false) — can_withdraw now false for USDC. USDC held 0.889M vs ledger-available 9.81M. This means the user's USDC is now frozen — withdrawals disabled.

- O16 (10:06): Guardian disables 17 assets total. Protocol-wide pause of asset capacities.

- O17 (14:08): Burrow DAO proposals to unregister margin dex (ref-exchange, ref-dcl), both approved. Response/remediation.

- O18 (14:55): CertiKAlert confirms incident: attacker created fake token contracts, added liquidity in fresh pools, misleading oracle and validation layer. ~$7.6M extracted.

Current time: 2026-04-16T14:55:14Z — same as O18.

Assessment:

The user has ~$1,000 native USDC supplied to Rhea Lend, no debt. The protocol has been exploited: ~$7.6M extracted. The token balances held by the contract are massively depleted: USDC held ~0.889M vs ledger-available 9.81M (~9% backing). The guardian has disabled all asset capacities including USDC — can_withdraw=false. So the user cannot withdraw right now even if they wanted to; the position is frozen.

Risk level: This is clearly critical. Active confirmed exploit affecting this exact venue and this exact asset (native USDC on contract.main.burrow.near). The contract holds only ~9% of the USDC it owes to suppliers. Withdrawals are disabled by the guardian. Confirmed loss of $7.6M.

Action: What can the keeper do? The actions are hold, reduce_light, reduce_to_target, exit, relever. The user cannot move funds — "you cannot move funds, only propose an action; the corridor limits enforce safety." So we propose exit — the desired action is to unwind the whole position now. Even though withdrawals are currently disabled (can_withdraw=false), the proposed action should be exit: attempt to withdraw/unwind the whole position now. If the corridor limits block it because withdrawals are disabled, that's enforced elsewhere. The correct risk signal is exit.

Alternatively, one might argue "hold" because withdrawal is impossible — but the framework says propose an action; exit is the right call for a critical incident affecting the position. The keeper should signal exit intent; corridor limits enforce safety (they'd block if impossible). Given the position is impaired and frozen, exit is the appropriate proposed action — attempting withdrawal as soon as capacities are re-enabled, and signaling maximal defensiveness.

Risk: critical.

Reasons:
- Confirmed exploit on Rhea Lend/Burrow: ~$7.6M extracted via fake tokens/fresh pools misleading oracle (CertiK).
- Onchain shows USDC held collapsed to ~9% of ledger-available (0.889M vs 9.81M); reserves wiped to zero; matches drain pattern from fresh-attacker-account margin positions through self-created Ref pools.
- Guardian disabled all capacities for native USDC (and 17 assets) — withdrawals frozen; position impaired/stuck.
- Official "funds are safe" message contradicted by onchain drain; treat as unreliable.
- DAO unregistering margin dexes confirms incident response.

Source ids: O05, O06, O07, O08, O09, O10, O12, O15, O16, O18. Maybe also O04 (false reassurance), O17. Keep it focused: the key drivers are O18 (confirmed exploit), O15/O16 (withdrawals disabled), O06/O07/O10/O12 (insolvency of held balances), O08/O09/O05 (attack mechanics on this contract).

Action: exit. Even though can_withdraw is currently false, the keeper proposes exit; corridor limits enforce what's possible. The position is directly impaired — held USDC is ~9% of liabilities — so full unwind is the only defensive action; partial trims don't make sense when the venue itself is compromised and frozen.
